reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Caused by deficiency of prolidase (peptidase D, encoded by PEPD), the enzyme that cleaves dipeptides with proline or hydroxyproline at the C-terminus, a final step in collagen turnover
The hallmark clinical feature is chronic, recalcitrant skin ulceration, especially of the lower legs, together with a characteristic facies and recurrent infections
The diagnostic biochemical signature is massive urinary excretion of imidodipeptides (proline- and hydroxyproline-containing dipeptides)
Splenomegaly, recurrent respiratory and skin infections, and variable intellectual disability may accompany the skin disease
Impaired recycling of proline from collagen breakdown is thought to compromise wound healing and connective tissue integrity
Management is largely supportive with meticulous wound care; topical approaches aiming to supply amino acids to ulcers have been explored
Inheritance is autosomal recessive with wide phenotypic variability, from near-asymptomatic to severe
British spelling applies (e.g. tumour, oedema) where relevant to descriptions
reference.pathophysiology: Prolidase hydrolyses dipeptides in which the C-terminal residue is proline or hydroxyproline, the last enzymatic step that releases these imino acids from collagen degradation for reuse in new collagen synthesis. When prolidase is deficient, imidodipeptides accumulate and are excreted in large amounts in the urine, while recycling of proline for collagen synthesis is impaired. The resulting defect in connective tissue turnover and wound healing underlies the chronic, poorly healing skin ulcers, and the dermatological and immune manifestations characteristic of the disorder.
additionalDifferentials: Chronic venous or arterial leg ulceration of other cause
Pyoderma gangrenosum and other inflammatory ulcerative dermatoses
Other genodermatoses with poor wound healing
Immunodeficiency with recurrent skin and respiratory infection
Systemic lupus erythematosus (some patients have lupus-like features)
additionalInvestigations: Urine amino acid and peptide analysis demonstrating marked imidodipeptiduria
Prolidase enzyme activity assay in erythrocytes, leucocytes, or fibroblasts
Molecular analysis of the PEPD gene
Skin biopsy and wound swabs to characterise ulcers and infection
Imaging or examination for splenomegaly and associated features
redFlags: Extensive or infected chronic ulceration with systemic sepsis risk
Recurrent severe respiratory infections suggesting significant immune compromise
Features of an associated autoimmune process such as lupus
reference.prognosis: The course is highly variable; skin ulceration is often chronic and difficult to heal and may cause substantial morbidity, while some individuals remain mildly affected. Recurrent infection can be a significant contributor to morbidity.
pitfalls: Managing leg ulcers as simple venous disease without considering a metabolic cause in atypical, treatment-resistant cases
Overlooking associated immunodeficiency and infection risk
Missing associated autoimmune or lupus-like features
Assuming a uniform severe phenotype, when presentation ranges widely
references: Nyhan, Atlas of Inherited Metabolic Diseases
management: Centre care on meticulous chronic wound management of the leg ulcers with debridement, appropriate dressings, compression and skin protection
Trial topical amino acid preparations such as proline- and glycine-containing ointments applied to ulcers to supply substrate for local collagen repair
Treat secondary bacterial infection of ulcers and recurrent skin and respiratory infections with culture-directed antibiotics
Undertake immunological assessment given recurrent infection and screen for the associated autoimmune, lupus-like manifestations
Monitor for splenomegaly, cytopenias and progressive dermatological disease at follow-up
Manage through a multidisciplinary team spanning dermatology, wound care, metabolic medicine and immunology
Provide genetic counselling and family screening, as the disorder is autosomal recessive
